events.title: First Modern Olympic Games Open in Athens
events.description: The first modern Olympic Games opened in Athens, Greece, at the Panathenaic Stadium. Organized by Pierre de Coubertin and the International Olympic Committee, the Games brought together athletes from 14 nations to compete in events such as track and field, swimming, and gymnastics.
events.significance: Revived the ancient Greek Olympic tradition and launched the international sporting event that has become the world's foremost athletic competition.

events.title: Robert Peary Claims Reaching the North Pole
events.description: American explorer Robert Peary, accompanied by Matthew Henson and four Inuit men, claimed to have reached the geographic North Pole after a grueling Arctic expedition. The claim has been disputed by historians and rival explorers.
events.significance: Marked one of the most celebrated and controversial achievements in the history of polar exploration.

events.title: United States Enters World War I
events.description: Following Congress's declaration of war against Germany, President Woodrow Wilson signed the war resolution on April 6, 1917. The decision followed unrestricted German submarine warfare and the Zimmermann Telegram.
events.significance: American entry shifted the balance of power in the war, bringing fresh troops and resources to the Allies and marking the emergence of the United States as a global military power.

events.title: Rwandan and Burundian Presidents Killed; Rwandan Genocide Begins
events.description: A plane carrying Rwandan President Juvénal Habyarimana and Burundian President Cyprien Ntaryamira was shot down near Kigali. The assassination triggered a campaign of mass violence by Hutu extremists against the Tutsi minority and moderate Hutus.
events.significance: Set off the Rwandan genocide, in which an estimated 500,000 to 800,000 people were killed in roughly 100 days, prompting lasting reflection on international inaction.

events.title: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints Organized
events.description: Joseph Smith and a small group of followers formally organized the Church of Christ in Fayette, New York, which later became The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.
events.significance: Founded one of the largest homegrown American religious movements, which now has millions of members worldwide.
